title: Experts’ View on Challenges and Needs for Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines the challenges and needs that educational AI researchers and practitioners identify when trying to make AI systems fairer. The central question is not whether a specific AI intervention improves student outcomes, but rather how fairness should be understood, monitored, and operationalized across the development pipeline of AI-based educational systems.

The authors used a two-step mixed-methods design. First, they conducted an anonymous online survey with 136 experts who had published at top educational technology venues in 2021, including AIED, EDM, ITS, EC-TEL, LAK, ICALT, EAAI, and L@S, plus related special issues. Second, they interviewed 28 survey respondents in semi-structured one-on-one interviews to deepen and validate the survey themes. Participants came from a diverse set of countries and represented researchers and practitioners working on educational AI.

The study identifies recurring concerns around data collection, demographic representation, local/contextual bias, fairness-aware modeling, transparency, auditing, and accountability. Participants emphasized that fairness should be considered continuously across the pipeline, not only at the model level, and that educational AI needs contextualized, domain-specific resources and tools. The paper concludes that fair educational AI requires better dataset practices, cross-institutional collaboration, participatory auditing, and multidisciplinary team awareness, especially because fairness issues in education are highly context dependent.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative/mixed-methods expert elicitation study with a clearly described sampling and analysis process, but it does not test an intervention or estimate causal effects. Evidence credibility is limited for impact claims because findings are based on expert perceptions rather than student-level outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has clear relevance for AI-in-education fairness practice and governance, but it reports no measurable learner or system effect sizes. Its impact is conceptual and institutional rather than demonstrating direct educational gains or harms.

interventions.use_case: expert survey and interviews on fairness challenges and needs in educational AI systems, including fairness auditing, dataset curation, and model governance

finding.finding_summary: This is a qualitative expert study, not an intervention outcome study. Across 136 survey respondents and 28 interviews, experts reported both strong perceived needs for fairness-oriented governance and substantial barriers to implementing it, including local context dependence, lack of standards, and uncertainty about accountability. No effect sizes were reported because the paper does not evaluate learner outcomes; it synthesizes practitioner views on fairness processes, auditing, and institutional responsibilities.
finding.measure: survey and interview themes on fairness needs, auditing, governance, and responsibilities
